facts.claim: Voyager 1 was launched by NASA on September 5, 1977, from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object from Earth, with a distance of over 15 billion miles (24.9 billion kilometers) as of early 2025.
Voyager 1 entered interstellar space on August 25, 2012, crossing the heliopause.
Voyager 1's velocity relative to the Sun is approximately 17 kilometers per second (38,000 mph).
Voyager 1 carries the Golden Record, a 12-inch gold-plated copper disk containing sounds and images selected to represent life on Earth.
The Voyager 1 mission was designed by a team led by project scientist Edward C. Stone (deceased in 2024) at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Voyager 1's power source is a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) that produces about 250 watts at launch, decaying over time.
In November 2023, Voyager 1 experienced a communication glitch, sending unusable data; engineers restored normal operations by April 2024.
Voyager 1 is expected to have enough power to operate its instruments until about 2025, after which it will continue traveling without scientific data.
Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Jupiter on March 5, 1979, revealing volcanic activity on the moon Io.
Voyager 1 made its closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980, studying Titan's thick atmosphere.
Voyager 1 is the only human-made object to have left the heliosphere, and as of 2024 it was about 22 light-hours from Earth.
The Voyager 1 mission is part of NASA's Voyager program, which originally included Voyager 2; both probes were designed to study the outer planets.
Voyager 1's signal transmission power is about 20 watts, similar to a refrigerator light bulb, but detected from billions of kilometers away using large antennas.
The total cost of the Voyager mission (including both probes) was approximately $865 million, in 1970s dollars, adjusted to about $3 billion today.

hook_ideas: A tiny whisper from 15 billion miles: how a 20-watt signal can cross the solar system.
The 'pale blue dot' photo: Voyager 1 turned back and captured Earth from 6 billion km away.
What will remain when Voyager 1 goes silent? The Golden Record as a time capsule.
The 2023 glitch that nearly lost contact with the most distant object ever launched.
misconceptions: Common misconception: Voyager 1 has left the solar system. In reality, it has entered interstellar space but is still under the Sun's gravitational influence and has not left the solar system (the Oort Cloud extends much further).
Another misconception: Voyager 1 is the fastest human-made object. That title belongs to the Parker Solar Probe, which reaches higher speeds (but not yet interstellar).
